insights: Real GoHighLevel AI voice agents can be built via an 'Ask AI' prompt that auto-generates all agent settings (voice speed, end-silence delay, voice temperature) in seconds rather than manual configuration.

Outbound AI calling on GoHighLevel requires a formal carrier-level verification process: submitting a government ID and business identity, plus compliance with opt-in TOS language checked against each lead-capture form before an outbound automation can legally dial a contact.

Voice cloning is built into the platform: a business owner or agent can clone their own voice from as little as 30 seconds of audio (full accuracy needs 1-2 minutes) and assign it to the AI agent for familiarity/trust.
The platform supports a 'multilingual agent' mode that auto-detects and switches languages mid-call (e.g., English/Spanish/French) but this doesn't work well combined with custom cloned voices.

The typical automation build pattern for outbound AI voice calling is: Form Submitted trigger -> 'Voice AI Outbound' action -> pick phone number -> save, meaning outbound calls are automatically triggered by lead form opt-ins rather than manually dialed.

It is explicitly stated that agencies/freelancers should NOT submit their own ID for a client's outbound verification -- the actual business owner must submit their own identity documents, or there is liability risk for the agency.
